svg.title: RIEMANN-MASULLO-DIAGRAMS D12 — Chapter 12 · Ch12_TraceGeometric, declaration by declaration
svg.desc: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 558 declarations of the 47 items on C12, each with its kind, file, line and state; 64 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted.

svg.text: riemann-masullo at 72a10ff: the 558 declarations of the 47 items on C12, each with its kind, file, line and state; 64 declarations with a Deviation: line, quoted.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Posters: M1, what the targets rest on · M2, the steps with no known repair · M3, the paper by depth · M4, every chapter · M5, the refutations. Names, items, files, entries and posters are links, underlined under the pointer: a card's title or a Lean name opens the source at the pin.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: How to read it. The expansion of C12's cards, in the same order: one block per item, its heading opening the card. First the declarations whose docstring states how the Lean departs from the print, each with its Deviation: line quoted from the Lean source (Apache-2.0), then every declaration of the item. A name opens its line at the

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: pin. A declaration's state is read from the terms: open when it uses sorryAx, resting when something open is below it. That a declaration states what its Deviation: line says is the docstring's claim, not checked here.

g.text: The printed proof does this in one display. The route is a partial Fourier inversion per place, discreteness of the S-units after dropping one place, the lift identity, and invariance of the principal values under u ↦ u⁻¹ (the last step on p. 519).

g.text: Uses the sharp expression from (12.4.1.24) with R = λλ′. The replacement of φ(g⁻¹) by φ(g) is the last step on p. 519. Appendix B.4 incorporates the real and complex normalization factors in the archimedean distributions.

g.text: The chosen quotient kernel must have integrable diagonals and agree asymptotically with the summed sharp masses. These hypotheses expose the missing comparison with the regularized Paley–Wiener operator. The limit is joint.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Footnote 2 on p. 514 requests a one-sided extension of Definition 9.3.3.1. Keep its parameter bounds and upper transition. For the ball in Step II, take the profile to be one from zero through L − ε and zero from L onwards. See sLocalTraceFourierCutoff and ERRATA F246.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: This is a fixed-level result with evaluation and integrability hypotheses. It gives no comparison with the sharp orbital masses as the levels change.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The operator on the level is assumed bounded, evaluation is assumed uniformly bounded and continuous, and the density is included in the measure μ. The cutoff is written as a square, with its square root in L².

g.text: Use positive representatives for the quotient by ±1, so even Schwartz tests give the level by sign averaging, up to a scalar. The two upper cutoffs are radial bumps, and the spatial one equals one near zero. …

g.text: The half-width is positive as in §1.8.4, p. 53. The global volume and the normalized complex denominator ‖1 − u‖² follow Theorem B.4.4.7 and (12.4.1.26). The all-width conclusion uses traceFormula_exteriorZeros.

g.text: The half-width is at least one half. The exterior is empty, so the test may take arbitrary values on the norm-one classes.

g.text: The half-width is at least one half and the test may be arbitrary. The global volume and the local coefficients follow Theorem B.4.4.7, p. 623.

g.text: Only F = ℚ, and Dirichlet GRH (the statement of DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf) is a hypothesis. The printed argument claims the cancellation unconditionally; it is the recorded gap traceFormula_exteriorZeros.

g.text: Only F = ℚ. This is the converse of traceFormula_exteriorZeros_rat_of_dirichletGRH: any proof of the gap over ℚ proves the statement of DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf.

text.tspan: · p. 520 · 32 declarations, 4 deviating from the print

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Definition 10.4.3.7 uses the tensor for convolution after projection. The right side is the trace computed by spectralStripConvolution_trace. It counts the closed strip with spectralStripMultiplicity. When the two edges contain no zeros this recovers the interior sum in (12.5.1.4).

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: The trace counts the closed strip with strict reciprocal-weight multiplicities on its two edges. If both edges are zero-free the sum is precisely the interior sum printed on p. 520.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: We ask for any representing tensor, restricted to the positive half-widths and tests of Theorem 12.5.1.1. We impose no finite-rank expansion on the tensor.

text.font-family: 'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'RD Noto Sans', 'RD Noto Sans Math', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: As in §12.5 of the library, a measurable D′-sequence specifies the smoothening, and the sum uses the closed strip with strict reciprocal-weight multiplicities on its edges. It agrees with the printed interior sum when both edges are zero-free. It is proved from the kernel existence statement above, which is open, so it is no more established than that statement. Nothing in the Lean
